title: Spark's minimum lending rate is the greater of the Sky Savings Rate plus 0.3% or SOFR
content:
Both of Spark's off-chain lending programs impose the same rate floor. For Arkis (A.6.1.1.1.3.7.2.4.2.2) and for Offchain Collateralized Lending (A.6.1.1.1.3.8.2.4.2.2), "the minimum borrow rate... must be **the greater of** the following at the time of issuance or renewal: Sky Savings Rate + 0.3%; SOFR."

The two terms encode two different ways a loan can be a mistake.

**SSR + 0.3%** is Sky's internal opportunity cost. Every dollar Spark lends is a dollar that could have retired sUSDS liabilities or funded savings vaults paying the SSR, so lending below it destroys value inside the ecosystem regardless of what the market offers. The 0.3% is the required compensation for taking counterparty and operational risk that holding the alternative does not carry.

**SOFR** is the external opportunity cost — the rate available on secured overnight dollar funding with no crypto exposure at all. A crypto-collateralized loan to a trading firm below SOFR is worse than a Treasury repo.

Taking the maximum means the floor automatically tracks whichever constraint binds. When Sky's rate is high, the internal test governs; when dollar rates rise faster, SOFR does. Neither can be arbitraged against the other.

The definitions (A.6.1.1.1.3.7.2.4.1.2, A.6.1.1.1.3.8.2.4.1.2) then leave the *form* completely open — "fixed rate, fixed spread vs a benchmark, performance fee or profit sharing based, or combination of the above" — while insisting "loans may not be issued with borrow cost structures below the values specified." Spark will accept upside-sharing economics and exotic structures; it will not accept them costing less than its own floor.
description: The floor is a maximum of two opportunity costs — Sky's own cost of funds plus margin, and the risk-free dollar rate — so no loan can be issued that underperforms either alternative.
